title: When the cost of each unit rises

predict.q: MB falls from 60; MC rises from 15. They cross at quantity 3. The cost of every unit rises by 15. What happens to the best quantity?

options.s: It stays at 3, because MB has not changed
options.fb: MB unchanged, but MC rose, so the crossing moves left. Every unit now costs more than before.

options.s: It falls, to where the new MC meets MB
options.fb: MC shifts up by 15 and meets MB at quantity 2, where MB = MC = 40.

options.s: It rises, to cover the higher cost
options.fb: Higher costs make each unit less worth doing; a rational chooser does fewer, not more.
The first units still have MB above the new MC (MB starts at 60, the new MC at 30), so doing some is still worth it.

task: Move the extra cost slider and watch the crossing point of MB and MC. Then try the MB intercept.

target.do: Move the extra cost slider to 15, then press Check.

takeaway: Anything that changes MB or MC moves the best choice; at the optimum, MB = MC.
